I want to break down the QK matrix further into query-positional versus key-token blocks to see if such a recency term actually exists.

If I can isolate the token directions that each head prefers, this could reveal something like word-position tracking: heads devoted to copying "last space" or "last newline" position would effectively track position-within-word or position-within-line, a structural feature likely useful across English, romaji, and code syntax alike.

I'm trying to see whether the key token direction for H0, H1, and H5 is shared, since that would suggest they're coordinating around the same token class rather than tracking different ones independently. If I can't directly identify whether it's space or newline, maybe I can infer it from how a downstream layer-1 head uses this positional information — e.g., matching the query's own "last newline position" against candidate keys would confirm line-tracking behavior, consistent with Python-style structure.

import numpy as np
np.set_printoptions(precision=3, suppress=True, linewidth=220)
def raw(l,j):
    s=slice(64*j,64*j+64); return W[f'W_q.{l}'][s],W[f'W_k.{l}'][s],W[f'W_v.{l}'][s],W[f'W_o.{l}'][:,s]
Wq,Wk,Wv,Wo=raw(0,2)
A2=Wq.T@Wk
u,s,vt=np.linalg.svd(A2)
P=np.linalg.qr(np.concatenate([u[:,:16],vt[:16].T],1))[0]
P=np.linalg.svd(P)[0][:,:np.sum(np.linalg.svd(P,compute_uv=False)>0.5)]
uv,sv,vvt=np.linalg.svd(Wv); T=vvt[:20].T
# orthogonalize T against P
T=T-P@(P.T@T); T=np.linalg.svd(T,full_matrices=False)[0]
Q,_=np.linalg.qr(np.concatenate([P,T],1))
R=np.eye(384)-Q@Q.T
print('dims P',P.shape[1],'T',T.shape[1])
b=W['ln1_b.0']
print('ln1_b.0 energy in P,T,rest: %.3f %.3f %.3f'%(np.linalg.norm(P.T@b)**2,np.linalg.norm(T.T@b)**2,b@R@b))
for j in range(6):
    Wq,Wk,Wv,Wo=raw(0,j); A=Wq.T@Wk; tot=np.linalg.norm(A)**2
    blocks=np.array([[np.linalg.norm(X.T@A@Y)**2 if X is not None else 0 for Y in [P,T]] for X in [P,T]])/tot
    restq=np.linalg.norm(R@A)**2/tot; restk=np.linalg.norm(A@R)**2/tot
    OV=Wo@Wv; to=np.linalg.norm(OV)**2
    print(f'H{j} QK blocks (q rows P,T ; k cols P,T):',blocks.round(3).tolist(),' q-rest %.2f k-rest %.2f'%(restq,restk),
          '| OV input P %.2f T %.2f rest %.2f'%(np.linalg.norm(OV@P)**2/to,np.linalg.norm(OV@T)**2/to,np.linalg.norm(OV@R)**2/to))
